findings.claim: A copy onto a path held by a trashed ghost can attach the new note to a Tag row already marked for deletion, so the copy can lose that frontmatter tag.
findings.impact: When the ghost was the destination drive's last carrier of a tag and the copied note names that tag, the expected result is a copy with no chip for it, a removed Tag row and a 200 response. The tag stays in the file on disk, and a later chip edit would drop it from the file.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/fileops.py:196-198 deletes the ghost, flushes, then calls cleanup_orphan_tags, which only marks orphans with db.delete at backend/app/services/tagops.py:116-117 and does not flush them. backend/app/database.py:38 sets autoflush=False, so load_tag_index at backend/app/services/tagops.py:65, reached from backend/app/services/fileops.py:336, still sees the row. backend/app/services/tagops.py:134-136 flushes first in retarget_file_tags for this hazard ('or a row about to be deleted gets attached'), and replace_file_tags has no such flush. Upload avoids it through db.flush at backend/app/services/upload.py:318. file_tags.tag_id is ON DELETE CASCADE at backend/app/models.py:28. Trash keeps the file on disk (backend/app/services/fileops.py:711), and _resolve_copy_filename at backend/app/services/fileops.py:222-225 avoids a path that exists on disk, so the ghost must have lost its disk file out of band. backend/tests/test_frontmatter_tags_on_create.py has no ghost case.
findings.repro: not_reproduced: this verifier cannot run code, and the final state after flush is inferred from reading the code and SQLAlchemy's unit-of-work ordering. Steps to run: on drive B, trash n.md carrying the only reference to tag alpha and remove its disk file; copy n.md with tags: [alpha] from drive A to the same path on B; inspect the copy's File.tags and B's Tag rows.

bucket_proposal.reason: This is normal use but needs a narrow state: a trashed row with its disk file removed out of band, and that row as the tag's last carrier. No declared invariant covers it.

findings.proposed_fix: Call db.flush() before load_tag_index on this path, or flush at the end of the trashed branch in resolve_db_path_conflict, and add a copy-over-ghost test.

specification_compliance: No spec or invariants file declares this change: docs/specs/INDEX.md has no frontmatter entry and the review directory has no invariants.md.
The docstring at backend/app/services/tagops.py:84-85 says registering a note never depends on its tags. A failed flush inside the swallowed block does not meet that promise.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Registering a note can rename the drive's shared Tag row, changing the displayed spelling on other notes (backend/app/services/tagops.py:72-76).
A copy onto a path held by a trashed ghost can lose a frontmatter tag whose row is pending deletion (V1).
regression_risks: Scan, upload, copy and create now share the case-variant rename and flush in replace_file_tags.
Each new Markdown file with frontmatter loads the drive's Tag index once during a scan (backend/app/services/scanner.py:758, backend/app/services/tagops.py:65).
Upload and create now sweep the drive's orphan Tag rows in the same transaction as registration (backend/app/services/upload.py:324, backend/app/routers/drives.py:893).
test_coverage: No test covers a failed id write-back with tags, an oversized or non-UTF-8 upload, the copy size gap, or a failed flush inside the projection.
Case-variant reuse is tested for scan and single registration only, and the shared-row test asserts the count but not the spelling.
The cross-drive copy test catches rows created on the source drive, but seeds no destination row and no copy-over-ghost case.
